# PLAYER tool reference — PLAYER and operator surfaces

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/generate-player-tool-reference.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

This page is generated directly from the canonical tool-player registries —
the SAME TypeBox parameter schemas a host binds and hands to an agent's
tool-calling loop. Every name, required/optional flag, type, default, and
description below is a tool's own runtime schema, not hand-copied prose: if a
tool's parameters change, this page changes with it
(the `player-tool-reference-drift` skgate registry gate fails the build
otherwise).

For the AUTHOR-facing verb surface (`spellkave_author_place`,
`spellkave_place_entity`, `spellkave_place_actor`, `spellkave_define_behavior`, …), see
[the world-author tool reference](../../spellkave-world-author/docs/tool-reference.md)
instead — a different registry, served to an authoring agent via
`spellkave_docs`. This page covers the PLAYER perceive/act surface and the
general/operator registry it's carved from, neither of which is served
through a docs-lookup tool today, so read this page as plain repo-browsable
markdown.

For the PLAYER role's own calling PATTERN (summary → list/targets → detail →
action), see [`../README.md`](../README.md).

## `spellkave_orient`

**Spellkave Orient** — execution mode `parallel`.

Rebuild your situation from the world in one call: self/scene/in-world turn-scene/manipulation and sensing facts plus inventory and the MOST RECENT page of traces — the one thing an actor with no history legitimately needs (a fresh conversation, a reloaded world, a restarted host). Freely callable mid-run too, as a situation refresh. Traces are bounded and page most-recent-first, never the whole history at once; pass the returned traces.next_cursor back as cursor to go further back, one page per call. view.manipulation_context uses the same snake_case rows as spellkave_manipulation_context (a prompts[] row from either is the same semantic_context); its actions are bounded to the most relevant rows (answers to open prompts first, then authored cues and defaults, then input forms, then alphabetical) with actions_total, actions_more and actions_by_niche saying what was left out — call spellkave_manipulation_context for more_action_ids (every other action id) and pass action_ids there for the syntax rows of named actions.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | no | string |  | Opaque traces.next_cursor from a prior spellkave_orient call — fetches the NEXT (older) page of traces. Omit for the first call: the most recent page, which stands alone as a usable orientation. |
| `limit` | no | number |  | Traces per page (default 10, max 25). Going further back costs more calls, deliberately — recall should cost turns, not one unbounded dump. |

## `spellkave_self_summary`

**Spellkave Self Summary** — execution mode `parallel`.

Compact directly-controlled character summary — the RECURRING glance you re-fetch often (vitals/quest/conditions/capabilities), not a one-time sheet. Identity is the connected actor; no actor id is accepted. `conditions`, `vitals`, `quest`, and `capabilities` are each a bounded-collection envelope: `listing` is "complete" when `items` holds the whole authorized collection, or "examples" when it is a bounded slice with a machine-readable `continuation` {tool, args} for the rest. `vitals` and `quest` are world-driven: which states appear (and in what order) depends on the character; a character with no quest-tracking states correctly shows an empty `quest` bucket. Call spellkave_self_states with kind=state for the full authorized state set. `capabilities` holds the actor's own trained/granted capabilities; call spellkave_self_states with kind=capability for the full authorized set. Recent evaluation history (own rolls and check outcomes) is not part of this summary — call spellkave_self_states with kind=evaluation for it; act-tool results already carry the roll from the action that produced it. Identity (species/class/background/…) is not part of this summary either — it is static character data, not something that changes turn to turn, so it lives at spellkave_self_states with kind=identity: fetch that ONCE at session start for the detailed "who am I", and rely on this summary for everything that actually changes.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|

## `spellkave_self_states`

**Spellkave Self Sheet** — execution mode `parallel`.

Page through the connected actor's authorized state pools, conditions, capabilities, identity facets, recent evaluation history, or action-economy channel spends. Use kind=condition for condition continuation, kind=capability for the actor's own trained/granted capabilities, kind=identity for the actor's own species/class/background tags (static session-entry detail, with descriptions where the world declared them; fetch this once at session start rather than on every turn), kind=evaluation for the actor's own recent check outcomes (status and any resolved rolls — e.g. what a check rolled), most-recent-first, kind=economy for the actor's own action-economy channel standing (per channel: current-window spent_ms/window_start_ms, plus the last spend's cost_ms/remaining_ms — "how much of my turn is left"). State rows support authored state-id prefix and exact resource-tag filters. Evaluation rows support an exact provenance_id filter to look up a specific record (e.g. from an act receipt). Use next_cursor to continue.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | no | string |  | Opaque next_cursor from the prior page. |
| `kind` | no | "state" \\| "condition" \\| "capability" \\| "evaluation" \\| "economy" \\| "economy_budget" \\| "identity" |  | Self-sheet row kind. Defaults to state. |
| `limit` | no | number |  | Rows per page. |
| `provenance_id` | no | string |  | Exact provenance_id filter; valid only for kind=evaluation. Returns matched 1 and the row, or matched 0. |
| `state_prefix` | no | string |  | Exact state_id prefix filter; valid only for kind=state. |
| `state_tag` | no | string |  | Exact authored resource tag filter; valid only for kind=state. |

## `spellkave_scene`

**Spellkave Scene** — execution mode `parallel`.

Orient on the connected actor's authorized current scene (location implicit). Unfiltered and under the bound, returns EVERY authorized target (`listing: "complete"`) alongside authored node prose (`node_description`, `graph_description`, `pose_elevation`) and occupant/entity/exit/trace `counts`. `graph_description` is carried only the first time this session sees the current region, or again after a call returns to a DIFFERENT region than the previous scene read — repeated reads within the same region carry `graph_description: null` instead of repeating the identical blurb. Add a `kind` filter, exceed the bound, or pass a `cursor` and it falls back to a flat, revision-bound paged list (`listing: "paginated"`) carrying the SAME handles and the SAME node prose/counts. Each `exit` row carries its destination as `to` (shortened when it stays in the same region — full path only across a region switch), so spellkave_scene_detail is only needed for an exit's extra detail, not to learn where it leads. Each item carries its OWN stable `handle`+`rev`: the SAME actor/entity/exit/trace keeps the SAME handle across scene re-reads and ticks, for as long as it exists, even while unrelated targets in the same scene change; `rev` gates freshness of that ONE target only. Follow up on any handle with spellkave_scene_detail or spellkave_move (rev+handle mode) by copying that item's OWN `rev`+`handle` verbatim — never the envelope's top-level `rev` — and the same stale_handle rejection applies at either: the loop closes at act, not at this observe call, and other actors may move between the two. While you are on a journey the answer is still the place you left and carries journey {status, arrives_in_ticks, arrives_at_tick}; pass wait_for_arrival_ms to wait for the arrival in one call instead of polling.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | no | string |  | Opaque next_cursor from the prior page. |
| `kind` | no | "actor" \\| "entity" \\| "exit" \\| "trace" |  | Optional scene target kind filter. |
| `limit` | no | number |  | Rows per page. |
| `wait_for_arrival_ms` | no | number |  | Optional. While you are on a journey (a move that takes several ticks), wait up to this many milliseconds for it to end, then answer with the scene as it is then. Returns at once when you are not travelling; the host may cap the wait, and journey_wait says how it ended. Use this instead of re-reading the scene or the session status until you arrive. |

## `spellkave_scene_detail`

**Spellkave Scene Detail** — execution mode `parallel`.

Read one current authorized scene target by its OWN rev+handle (copy both verbatim from that target's own listing row — not the listing envelope's top-level `rev`). The handle is a stable identity: the SAME exit/actor/entity/trace keeps the SAME handle across arbitrarily many scene re-reads and ticks, for as long as it exists, even while unrelated targets in the same scene change. `rev` gates freshness of that ONE target only — a rev mismatch (`stale_handle`) means THIS target's own content changed since the handle was issued; a handle that no longer resolves at all (`unknown_handle`) means the target left this actor's authorized scene (moved away, removed, out of range). An `actor` target's `detail` additionally carries `description` (authored flavor prose, `""` if none), `appearance` (the public appearance text the character wrote at creation, `""` if none), `entity_def_id` (its authored definition id — the SAME field the `entity` scene target already carries, `""` if unresolved), and `conditions` (the SAME visibility-filtered status effects `spellkave_self_states kind=condition` surfaces for the connected actor's own body, `[]` if none). Two addressing modes: {handle, rev} copied from the listing (freshness-gated), or target_id — the same typed id spellkave_manipulate takes (entity:156, item:157, actor:7) — which reads the current row and returns its rev. Entity and actor detail includes contents {container_ref, scope: "direct", revision, status, items}; status is available, empty, unavailable or truncated, with no hidden total. Items carry canonical item:N target_ref, parent_ref, name, quantity and entity_def_id. Inspect a disclosed child with target_id, including nested containers; these children do not become room occupants. Contents changes affect the target revision, and closing an ancestor revokes its descendants. Visibility does not promise pickup success or grant personal inventory state.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `handle` | no | string |  | Stable scene target handle, e.g. s:exit:32 or s:actor:7 — copied from spellkave_scene. Pass with rev, or pass target_id instead. |
| `rev` | no | string |  | With handle: the target's OWN rev, copied verbatim from its row in spellkave_scene — not the listing envelope's top-level rev (stable per-target handles, freshness gated per target). Omit when addressing by target_id. |
| `target_id` | no | string |  | Alternative addressing, the same typed id spellkave_manipulate and spellkave_communicate take (entity:156, item:157, actor:7): reads a current scene target or an item:N child disclosed through an exposed container, and returns its rev. One of {handle, rev} or target_id. |

## `spellkave_map`

**Map** — execution mode `parallel`.

Render the connected actor's OWN known map as the shared spatial view — fog-of-war scoped by the module's visible_place_* views (known places plus the current place's exit frontier). Routes admitted by the module are drawn; spellkave_scene stays the authority on what exits exist from the CURRENT place. output_type picks the ONE artifact computed and returned: 'utf8' box-drawing text, 'ascii' 7-bit text, 'braille' dense-dot text, 'inventory' the place/route listing alone, 'svg' (default) the raw picture (plus an inline picture for hosts that render tool images), 'jpg' a backdrop-composed map-art JPEG written to disk (details.jpg_path). On the hosted PLAYER MCP gateway, results may also include one text line linking to the interactive browser map (maps.spellkave.com/?world=<slug>) for this world. While you are in a fight with a tactical grid drawn, the response also carries session_tokens: one row per roster participant placed on a drawn cell (node_id, actor_id, name, and is_me for your own row) — absent outside a fight, an empty list the moment the fight opens but before anyone has taken a cell.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `compose_parent` | no | boolean |  | Default true. When the selected map is a battle grid (including an automatically selected one), the grid draws composed over its parent location's own known layout (and, for output_type='jpg', the parent's backdrop art too) — one picture, the battle grid in room context. Has no effect for a non-grid map. Set false for the grid alone when you specifically want just the battle grid with no surrounding room. |
| `graph` | no | string |  | Optional map id — when set, draw that map restricted to places the connected actor has already seen. Omit and the map picks for you: while you are in a fight that opened a tactical grid, it draws THAT grid composed over the location you are fighting in (backdrop art plus the room's own layout, combat cells on top); otherwise it composes every known outdoor map. Naming a map explicitly always wins — pass the location's own id to see the region while a fight is open, or compose_parent=false for the bare grid. |
| `output_dir` | no | string |  | output_type='jpg' only; ignored otherwise. Host-supplied directory to write the map-art JPEG into — absolute, or RELATIVE to the host process's own cwd. A relative value resolves against process.cwd for the write, and is echoed back UNCHANGED — never resolved — in details.jpg_path, so a caller recording a portable artifact never leaks its own machine-local checkout path. Optional: omit for a fresh temp directory — a caller that just wants 'a JPEG, anywhere' does not have to invent a path. Backdrop art is drawn in full (the map on top stays scoped to places already seen, but the backdrop itself is NOT masked, so it may show rooms not yet discovered). |
| `output_name` | no | string |  | output_type='jpg' only; ignored otherwise. Base filename (no extension) for the JPEG written under output_dir, e.g. 'arrival'. Optional: omit for a name derived from graph, or 'map' when graph itself is also omitted. |
| `output_type` | no | "utf8" \\| "ascii" \\| "braille" \\| "inventory" \\| "svg" \\| "jpg" |  | Which single artifact to render — the engine computes ONLY this one. 'utf8' box-drawing text, 'ascii' 7-bit text, 'braille' dense-dot text — each returned in the like-named details field. 'inventory' skips the picture entirely, details.inventory only. 'svg' (default) returns the raw SVG string in details.svg (and, when the host renders tool-result images, an inline picture). 'jpg' writes a backdrop-composed JPEG to output_dir/output_name and returns its path as details.jpg_path — no svg/ascii/utf8/braille text in the response at all. |
| `slice` | no | "elevation_band" \\| "all_floors_offset" \\| "topology_only" \\| "metric" \\| "h3_world" |  | How to project multi-floor / unpositioned maps: elevation_band (one floor), all_floors_offset (floors side-by-side), topology_only (adjacency layout), metric (all z in one plane), h3_world (outdoor maps laid out geographically). Omit for auto. |
| `z` | no | number |  | Elevation for slice=elevation_band. Omit to use the anchor floor for a battle grid composed over its parent location; otherwise defaults to 0. An explicit z always wins. |
| `z_tolerance` | no | number |  | Half-width of elevation_band in elevation units (default 0.5). |

## `spellkave_move`

**Spellkave Move** — execution mode `sequential`.

Move the active actor — exactly one addressing mode per call. Preferred: {rev, handle}, a stable-identity scene exit handle copied VERBATIM (both fields) from that exit's own row in spellkave_scene — the SAME exit keeps the SAME handle across re-reads and ticks; `rev` gates freshness of that ONE exit only, never the whole scene. Compatibility: {edge_id}, an adjacent-exit identifier when you do not have a scene handle. Movement is ATTEMPT-based: every exit is tried, and the world gives the authoritative verdict. The scene listing's `traversal_gates` and this tool's own `traversal_gates` echo (rev+handle mode only) are map info about what LOOKED likely, never permission. In rev+handle mode, the result carries `receipt` (what the world did) and a sibling `observation` (prose of what the actor perceived — an authored node description, or the region's own description only when the move crossed into a different region, never repeated within the same one — or null + observation_gap when no authorized source backs this outcome); a rejection carries `receipt.move.reason` and `receipt.move.failure_detail`, never a throw. In edge_id mode, the result is a flatter `{status, actor_id, edge_id, from_node, to_node, observed_at_tick}` shape, with `reason`/`failure_detail` on rejection. Movement is never turn-gated: a move may be accepted even while `my_turn` is false. In rev+handle mode, on an ADMITTED dispatch (an immediate arrival OR a promoted long-running 'travelling' walk) with a host world-event builder wired, the result also carries `consequences`: same-tick, same-transaction WorldEvents THIS move deterministically caused (e.g. a travel-cost resource spend) — a THIRD register, distinct from `receipt`/`observation` (the reducer's own outcome) and from a LATER `pushes` drain off the same builder (world news, including this move's own delayed arrival). Omitted entirely when no builder is wired; `[]` when wired but nothing was caused. A move longer than your reach returns outcome "travelling" and takes several ticks: pass wait_for_arrival_ms to wait for the arrival in the same call, or spellkave_scene with wait_for_arrival_ms to keep waiting; do not poll.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `as_body_id` | no | string |  | Observed non-presence body to act as using frontier.impersonate; the server checks scope and consent. |
| `control_token` | no | object |  |  |
| `edge_id` | no | string |  | Adjacent-exit mode: identifier of an adjacent exit from where you are. Prefer rev+handle instead — this mode exists when you do not have a scene handle. |
| `handle` | no | string |  | Scene-handle mode: stable scene exit handle, e.g. s:exit:32, from spellkave_scene. Required together with rev; omit both and pass edge_id instead for the adjacent-exit mode. |
| `rev` | no | string |  | Scene-handle mode: the exit's OWN rev, copied verbatim from its row in spellkave_scene — not the listing envelope's top-level rev. Required together with handle; omit both and pass edge_id instead for the adjacent-exit mode. |
| `wait_for_arrival_ms` | no | number |  | Optional, scene-handle mode. A move longer than your reach becomes a journey of several ticks (outcome "travelling"). With this field the call waits up to that many milliseconds for the journey to end and then returns the arrival observation; journey says whether you arrived, were stopped elsewhere, or are still travelling (the host may cap the wait). Without it the call returns as soon as the journey starts. |

#### `control_token`

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `actor_id` | yes | string |  |  |
| `body_entity_id` | yes | string |  |  |
| `generation` | yes | string |  |  |
| `world_instance_id` | yes | string |  |  |

## `spellkave_inventory`

**Spellkave Inventory** — execution mode `parallel`.

Orient on the connected actor's authorized carried inventory. Unfiltered and under the bound, returns a grouped tree of top-level possessions with nested `contents` and `equipped_slot` markers. Add a kind/name_prefix filter, exceed the bound, or pass a cursor and it falls back to a flat, revision-bound paged list carrying the SAME handles the tree uses. Every response self-describes via `listing` ('complete' for the tree, 'paginated' for the flat fallback). Each item carries its OWN stable `handle`+`rev`: the SAME item keeps the SAME handle across re-reads, for as long as it exists, regardless of tree position or what else in the inventory changed. Follow up on any handle with spellkave_item_detail by copying that item's OWN `rev`+`handle` verbatim — never the envelope's top-level `rev`.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | no | string |  | Opaque next_cursor from a prior paged response. Forces the flat paged list. |
| `kind` | no | string |  | Optional exact authored entity kind filter. Forces the flat paged list. |
| `limit` | no | number |  | Maximum items per page, and the unfiltered grouped-tree threshold. Defaults to 50. |
| `name_prefix` | no | string |  | Optional case-insensitive item-name prefix filter. Forces the flat paged list. |

## `spellkave_item_detail`

**Spellkave Item Detail** — execution mode `parallel`.

Inspect one item selected by its OWN rev+handle from spellkave_inventory (copy both verbatim from that item's own row — not the listing envelope's top-level `rev`). The handle is the item's stable identity: the SAME item keeps the SAME handle across re-reads, for as long as it exists, regardless of tree position or what else in the inventory changed. Returns authorized identity, quantity, containment/equipment role, and owned state in one call; arbitrary item ids are not accepted. Two addressing modes: {handle, rev} copied from the listing (freshness-gated), or target_id — the same typed id spellkave_manipulate takes (entity:156, item:157, actor:7) — which reads the current row and returns its rev.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `handle` | no | string |  | Stable inventory item handle, e.g. i:42 — copied from spellkave_inventory. Pass with rev, or pass target_id instead. |
| `rev` | no | string |  | With handle: the item's OWN rev, copied verbatim from its row in spellkave_inventory — not the listing envelope's top-level rev (stable per-item handles, freshness gated per item). Omit when addressing by target_id. |
| `target_id` | no | string |  | Alternative addressing, the same typed id spellkave_manipulate takes (item:157 or entity:157): the current inventory row for that item is read without a rev, and its rev is returned. One of {handle, rev} or target_id. |

## `spellkave_trace_detail`

**Spellkave Trace Detail** — execution mode `parallel`.

Read one currently perceived trace by its OWN rev+handle (copy both verbatim from that trace's own row — not the listing envelope's top-level `rev`). The handle is the trace's stable identity: the SAME trace keeps the SAME handle across re-reads, for as long as it stays perceivable, regardless of what else was inscribed since. Returns parsed payload, never the raw payload JSON carrier.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `handle` | yes | string |  | Stable trace handle, e.g. t:4 — copied from spellkave_traces. |
| `rev` | yes | string |  | The trace's OWN rev, copied verbatim from its row in spellkave_traces — not the listing envelope's top-level rev (stable per-trace handles, freshness gated per trace). |

List the connected actor's OPEN post-roll intervention windows — a time-boxed pause after one of the actor's own stochastic actions, before the outcome commits. `faces` are the already-drawn, already-visible die face(s) for that action (two faces when the roll had Advantage/Disadvantage, otherwise one). The window closes on its own (equivalent to declining) if not answered before window_closes_at_micros. Respond with spellkave_react_option using this listing's handle: omit selected_draw_index to decline (the original result stands, nothing is spent), or pass the index of one listed face to accept (spends this window's fuel resource and replaces exactly that face — the new roll must then be used).

## `spellkave_react_option`

**Spellkave React Option** — execution mode `sequential`.

Execute one current handle for the connected actor — either a multi-actor reaction seat from spellkave_reaction_options, or a post-roll intervention window from spellkave_intervention_windows. For an intervention-window handle, omit selected_draw_index to decline (keep the original result, spend nothing) or pass the index of one of that window's listed faces to accept (spends its fuel resource and replaces exactly that face; the new roll must then be used). The handle only selects; the world independently revalidates sender, eligibility, and the window. On dispatch, the result carries `receipt` (what the world did) and a sibling `observation` (prose of what the actor perceived, or null + observation_gap when no authorized source backs this outcome). On a SUCCESSFUL dispatch with a host world-event builder wired, the result also carries `consequences`: same-tick, same-transaction WorldEvents THIS reaction deterministically caused — a THIRD register, distinct from `receipt`/`observation` (the reducer's own outcome) and from a LATER `pushes` drain off the same builder (world news, e.g. another agent's subsequent move). Omitted entirely when no builder is wired; `[]` when wired but nothing was caused.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `handle` | yes | string |  | A handle from spellkave_reaction_options (e.g. r2) or spellkave_intervention_windows (e.g. w0). |
| `response_intent` | yes | string |  | Authored or free-text response intent passed to the typed reaction reducer. |
| `rev` | yes | string |  | Current reaction-window or intervention-window revision (matches the handle's domain). |
| `selected_draw_index` | no | number |  | Intervention windows only: the index (into that window's `faces`) of the already-drawn face to replace. Omit to decline — the original result stands and nothing is spent. Providing an index accepts: it spends the window's fuel resource and replaces exactly that one face; the new roll must then be used. Ignored (and should be omitted) for a plain spellkave_reaction_options seat. |

## `spellkave_manipulation_context`

**Spellkave Manipulation Context** — execution mode `parallel`.

Read your additive factored manipulation context: shared authored action syntax, independently observed typed targets, and complete participant expectations. These are neutral discovery facts, not a list of action-target offers and not a promise that an attempt will succeed. Use them to compose one typed manipulation attempt; the world authoritatively reselects and validates it against fresh state. The default answer is a bounded summary: prompts[], targets[], participants[], the most relevant action rows in actions[] (answers to open prompts first, then authored cues and defaults, then input forms, then alphabetical), and more_action_ids naming every other action you may attempt. Pass action_ids to read the syntax rows of named actions; detail="full" returns the whole registry and is large. prompts[] lists the open dialogue prompts you may answer now (question, labels, responseActionIds; multi-pick questions state the remaining picks, this one included); answering one means sending its responseActionId with that row as args_json {"semantic_context": <row>}. A prompt opens one to three ticks after the answer that leads to it; pass wait_for_prompt_ms to wait for it in one call instead of polling. It waits for a prompt only: it is not a way to wait for a journey or a turn.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `action_ids` | no | array<string> |  | Optional, summary only: action ids (from more_action_ids, a prompt's response_action_ids, or a hint) whose syntax rows to return first in actions[]. Ids the listing does not hold come back in unknown_action_ids. |
| `as_body_id` | no | string |  | Observed non-presence body to act as using frontier.impersonate; the server checks scope and consent. |
| `detail` | no | "summary" \\| "full" |  | Optional, default "summary": prompts[], targets[], participants[], the most relevant action rows (answers to open prompts first, then authored cues and defaults, then input forms, then alphabetical) as composition syntax, and more_action_ids naming every other action. "full" returns every action row with provider flags, template ids, groups and tags; it grows with the actor's capabilities (100 KB for a spellcaster) and is meant for programmatic readers. |
| `wait_for_prompt_ms` | no | number |  | Optional. When prompts[] holds no open, unanswered prompt yet, wait up to this many milliseconds for one to open before returning (a prompt opens one to three ticks after the answer that leads to it). Returns as soon as one opens, or at the deadline with prompts[] as it is then; the host may cap the wait. Omit for an immediate read. |

## `spellkave_traces`

**Spellkave Traces** — execution mode `parallel`.

Orient on perceived traces at the connected actor's current node (location implicit). Items are MOST-RECENT-FIRST (highest inscribed_at first) — page 0 is what just happened here, matching spellkave_orient.traces; pass next_cursor to walk further back. Unfiltered and under the bound, returns EVERY perceived trace (`listing: "complete"`) alongside a capped-and-truthful `by_kind` histogram (`kind_groups_total`/`kind_groups_shown`/`kind_groups_truncated`) computed over ALL perceived traces at this node, regardless of any filter you pass. Add a `kind`/`kind_prefix`/`inscribed_by`/`visibility` filter, exceed the bound, or pass a `cursor` and it falls back to a flat, revision-bound paged list (`listing: "paginated"`) carrying the SAME handles, node id, and the SAME global `by_kind` histogram — filtering `items` never narrows `by_kind`. Raw payload JSON is never returned; use spellkave_trace_detail for parsed payload. Each item carries its OWN stable `handle`+`rev`: the SAME trace keeps the SAME handle across re-reads for as long as it stays perceivable, and `rev` gates freshness of that ONE trace only — copy both verbatim into spellkave_trace_detail, not the envelope's top-level `rev`.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | no | string |  | Opaque next_cursor from the prior page. |
| `inscribed_by` | no | string |  | Optional exact inscriber id. |
| `kind` | no | string |  | Optional exact authored trace kind. |
| `kind_prefix` | no | string |  | Optional authored trace-kind prefix. |
| `limit` | no | number |  | Rows per page. |

## `spellkave_communicate`

**Spellkave Communicate** — execution mode `sequential`.

Attempt one authored speech act against one typed target. Use an observed participant or world target and an authored speech_act_id; the world authoritatively validates fresh state. An accepted utterance is echoed, may observe one bounded reply, and leaves later speech delivery in pushes. A prompt-bound answer (args_json.semantic_context), or an utterance on an action that carries an authored input form (a name or text field), also returns the next open prompt row as receipt.next_prompt, waited for inside the same reply window plus a short grace after the reply, so the next answer needs no manipulation_context read; next_prompt.status says whether a row opened, was already open, or timed out. An action's input.fields[].channel (from spellkave_manipulation_context) says how a field travels: "utterance" fields are read from what you say (plain text for one field, a JSON object keyed by field name for several); sending them in args_json is refused as utterance_required before dispatch.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `args_json` | no | string |  | Optional JSON argument blob, passed 1:1 to the world. Defaults to '{}'. For an authored session opener, participant_entity_ids is a nonempty list of up to 64 distinct runtime body ids; the session definition and grid remain authored, and older modules refuse this argument before dispatch. For an action that creates an entity, definition_ref names an allowed definition; the world checks the choice against the action's authored limits. A prompt-bound answer (a speech_act_id listed in a prompts[] row's responseActionIds in spellkave_manipulation_context, e.g. dm/dialog/choice/2) must carry that prompts[] row here as {"semantic_context": <row>}; without it the world rejects the answer with prompt_context_required. |
| `speech_act_id` | yes | string |  | Speech-act identifier to perform. |
| `target_id` | yes | string |  | Typed target reference to communicate with — use an observed participant or location reference (e.g. 'entity:42'). The world authoritatively validates the attempt; a bare numeric id is ambiguous and may be rejected or misresolved. |
| `utterance` | no | string |  | Optional words to say. On acceptance they are delivered to the world as dispatch_text, echoed in the receipt, and may open the bounded reply window. |

## `spellkave_end_turn`

**Spellkave End Turn** — execution mode `sequential`.

End the connected actor's current turn in the in-world turn/scene (not the MCP connection), without supplying a session id. The world resolves active participation and rejects no-session/off-turn calls (`no_session` still allows exploration; or it is not your turn). NOTE: advancing the turn does NOT refresh the new current actor's available actions — only turn-gated (action-economy) rows are recomputed on a turn boundary; other available actions stay whatever they were. Movement is unaffected either way: spellkave_scene's exits are always current, so they are never stale from a missed refresh. On dispatch, the result carries `receipt` (what the world did) and a sibling `observation` (a fixed 'Your turn ends.' line on success, or 'Nothing happens.' on rejection). On a successful advance, the receipt also carries the NEW in-world `session` block (`in_session`/`current_actor`/`my_turn`) — whose turn it is next in that scene, not the MCP connection.

## `spellkave_manipulate`

**Spellkave Manipulate** — execution mode `sequential`.

Attempt one authored action against one typed target. Prefer action_id and target_id from spellkave_manipulation_context when it is ready; those facts support composition but never promise success. Direct typed attempts remain allowed and the world authoritatively validates fresh state. Args pass 1:1 and success is provenance-observed. For a prompt-bound dialog answer (a prompts[] row, dm/dialog/choice/N) or any free-text creation field use spellkave_communicate instead: it carries the utterance and returns the next open prompt row on its receipt; this tool does not. A field whose input.fields[].channel is "utterance" cannot be sent here: the attempt is refused as utterance_required and names the spellkave_communicate speech act to use.

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| `action_id` | yes | string |  | Open authored action identifier to attempt against the target — prefer action_id from spellkave_manipulation_context when it is ready; it is discovery data, not an eligibility guarantee. |
| `args_json` | no | string |  | Optional JSON argument blob, passed 1:1 to the world. Defaults to '{}'. For an authored session opener, participant_entity_ids is a nonempty list of up to 64 distinct runtime body ids; the session definition and grid remain authored, and older modules refuse this argument before dispatch. For an action that creates an entity, definition_ref names an allowed definition; the world checks the choice against the action's authored limits. May include participant_context (an mpc:<id> token from spellkave_manipulation_context.participants) when the action has more than one disclosed participant binding. A prompt-bound action (an action_id listed in a prompts[] row's responseActionIds in spellkave_manipulation_context) must carry that prompts[] row here as {"semantic_context": <row>}; without it the world rejects the attempt with prompt_context_required. |
| `as_body_id` | no | string |  | Observed non-presence body to act as using frontier.impersonate; the server checks scope and consent. |
| `control_token` | no | object |  |  |
| `participant_context` | no | string |  | Optional mpc:<id> token from spellkave_manipulation_context.participants for this action. Required when the ready context lists more than one participant row for the action (e.g. Load with two bolts). May also be placed inside args_json; the two must agree. |
| `target_id` | yes | string |  | Typed target reference to manipulate — prefer target_ref from spellkave_manipulation_context when it is ready (e.g. 'entity:42', 'item:7'). Direct typed attempts remain allowed; the world authoritatively validates them. A bare numeric id is ambiguous (defaults to entity) and will misresolve a contained item's location, e.g. rejecting a self-targeted item use as out_of_range . A carried item is an item: target; the inventory handle 'i:7' is read as 'item:7'. |

## 2. PLAYER-facing subset — `playerFacingToolDefinitions`

The exact tool set an actual PLAYER-role agent gets, in registration order
(`createPlayerFacingTools(context)`). Every entry is one of section 1's own
tools — follow the link to its full schema; membership itself is exported by
the registry (`PLAYER_FACING_TOOL_NAMES`), never re-curated by a consumer.
Do not hardcode a roster length in this heading — it goes stale (sk-jay0.7.15.7).
